claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch if the audit packet explicitly discloses the known retirement-plan-servicing weakness, despite the affected segment remaining in the initial rollout cohort and the current risk-acceptance draft being incomplete.
decision_criteria: If policy allows certification with a disclosed material limitation even while the affected use case remains exposed, and the disclosure is completed and binding before launch, the verdict could improve.
If an approved risk acceptance exists covering the exposed retirement-servicing weakness, the policy gap would narrow materially.
If the affected retirement-servicing use case is actually excluded from the rollout cohort, the rollout controls would better satisfy the stated policy.
If none of those conditions is met, certification remains inadequately supported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying text or approved record for ISTRESS-ROLLOUT-MONITORING-031-POLICY, especially the exact certification threshold when a material limitation is disclosed but unresolved.
Provide the actual model card or launch packet showing the retirement-plan-servicing hardship-withdrawal limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide the cohort definition and launch controls showing whether the affected retirement-servicing use case is included or excluded from the initial rollout.
Provide the current risk-acceptance record, approval status, and scope, or confirmation that no approved risk acceptance exists.
Provide the underlying readiness and rehearsal evidence supporting the aggregate pass margin and no-severity-one claim.
specific_concerns: The available support is second-hand only; I do not have the underlying admissible evidence, only the Actor's summary of it.
The governing policy expressly says rollout controls do not cure disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.

The Actor asserts certification is still defensible, but the summary does not provide the actual release-policy text showing that disclosure alone is sufficient for certification in this circumstance.
The current risk-acceptance draft is described as incomplete and not covering the exposed retirement-servicing use case, leaving a key policy predicate unresolved.
There is no admissible evidence here that the promised model-card disclosure has been completed, reviewed, or made a binding launch condition.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record, rather than merely arguable, is not established by the evidence available to me.
That explicit model-card disclosure will in fact occur before launch is unsupported in the materials available to me.

That aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, and staged rollout are sufficient to support certification for an exposed below-target segment is unsupported under the stated policy without additional evidence.
